Tomorrow I just ladle it straight onto the griddle while my coffee brews. Fresh pancakes with zero measuring before sunrise. What do you think?
samples.text:
Thank you for sharing your breakfast strategy. While pre-mixing batter is a common idea, storing a complete batter with baking powder in the refrigerator overnight often leads to disappointing results. The leavening agent begins to react immediately upon contact with the liquid, and by morning, the bubbles have dissipated. This typically causes the pancakes to rise quickly at first and then collapse, resulting in a dense, flat texture rather than the light, fluffy consistency you desire.

To achieve fresh-tasting pancakes with minimal morning effort, I recommend a make-ahead approach that separates the wet and dry ingredients. You can measure and mix the flour, sugar, and baking powder in an airtight container the night before. Simultaneously, whisk the eggs, milk, and any fat together in a separate sealed container. In the morning, you simply pour the wet mixture into the dry mixture and stir gently until just combined. This preserves the leavening power, ensuring your pancakes rise properly while still saving you valuable time during your busy weekday mornings.
